headline: Meaning isn't found—it's made
universal_truth: A meaningful life is built through connection, contribution, and presence
fun_facts: Psychologist Martin Seligman identified five pillars of well-being: positive emotion, engagement, relationships, meaning, and accomplishment
Research shows that people who prioritize meaning over happiness often end up experiencing more of both
Studies indicate that acts of service activate the brain's reward centers more powerfully than receiving rewards
discussion_questions: What moments in your life have felt most meaningful?
How do you know when something matters to you?
What would change if you designed your days around meaning instead of productivity?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: We all want our lives to matter. But here's the thing: meaning isn't hiding somewhere, waiting to be found. It's constructed—through choices, connections, and what we pay attention to. Today we explore how to build a meaningful life.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Most people chase happiness directly. But research shows a counterintuitive path: chasing meaning leads to deeper happiness than chasing happiness itself. Why might that be?
cliff.prompt: Why does pursuing meaning lead to happiness?

options.response: Exactly. Happiness without meaning is fragile. Meaning provides the bedrock that sustains us through difficulty.
They overlap, but they're distinct. Happiness is how you feel. Meaning is why you feel it matters.

q1.title: The Three Sources
q1.script: Research identifies three consistent sources of meaning: connection—mattering to others; contribution—making a difference; and coherence—seeing your life as part of a larger story. When these three align, life feels significant.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Three Sources"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Meaning Through Difficulty
q2.script: Paradoxically, some of our most meaningful experiences are difficult ones. Raising children, pursuing mastery, supporting loved ones through hardship—these aren't easy, but they matter deeply. Meaning often lives on the other side of effort.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Attention Choice
q3.script: What you pay attention to becomes your life. Two people can live identical circumstances and experience vastly different levels of meaning based on what they notice. Meaning is partly a function of where you aim your awareness.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You don't discover meaning like buried treasure. You create it through what you commit to, who you love, and how present you are. Your life already contains the ingredients—it's up to you to combine them.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's today's lesson on what makes life matter. Tomorrow, we'll explore how to decide right from wrong. Until then, notice where meaning already lives in your day.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Meaning Mapping - The Three Sources
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify how connection, contribution, and coherence show up in your life
growTrack.activity: Draw three columns: Connection, Contribution, Coherence. List one thing in each column that currently gives your life meaning. Reflect on which column needs more attention.
